newsitem.title: GABON: Gabon government vote for longer presidential term.
newsitem.headline: Gabon government vote for longer presidential term.

text.p: Gabon's government has approved a draft law to extend the term of future presidents from five to seven years and to create the post of vice-president, a government spokesman said.

A cabinet meeting on Thursday also voted to turn the senate, a new second house of parliament designed to promote a balance of power in the Central African oil-producing nation, into an upper rather than a lower chamber.
Parliament, where President Omar Bongo's supporters hold a majority in both houses, must approve the draft law.

Gabon held parliamentary elections in December and municipal elections in October. The opposition Woodcutters Rally did better in the municipal than in the legislative elections, winning control of the capital Libreville.

The elections were part of constitutional and electoral reforms launched after the oil-producing nation's political rivals struck a 1994 deal in Paris to defuse bloody unrest following Bongo's disputed 1993 election.
Bongo has ruled the former French colony since 1968 after the death of founding head of state, Leon Mba. He bowed to pressure for democratic reform in 1990. His presidential term ends in 1998.

Under the proposed changes, the president will nominate the vice-president and can sack him. Other changes envisage extending the parliament's year from six to eight months and giving it greater power to organise its own affairs.
